name: Anarchism
summary: Anarchism is the political philosophy and movement that seeks to abolish the state, capitalism and other institutions of coercive hierarchy, replacing them with voluntary, self-managed associations federated from the bottom up. Its mainstream, social anarchism, calls for common ownership of the means of production, workers' self-management and, in its communist form, the end of money and wage labour, reached through revolution and direct action rather than elections. It is internationalist, anti-militarist and generally secular, and it extends its critique of domination to patriarchy, nationalism and borders.
scope: The mainstream social anarchist tradition: the classical thinkers Proudhon, Bakunin, Kropotkin and Malatesta and the anarchist workers' movement, with contemporary positions as set out in An Anarchist FAQ and current scholarship (SEP, Uri Gordon). Where strands differ, answers follow the social anarchist majority. Individualist, mutualist, pacifist, religious, green and primitivist strands are noted but not followed, and anarcho-capitalism, which most anarchists do not accept as anarchism, is excluded; separate profiles exist for these strands.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Anarchists want healthcare freely available to all, but through mutual aid and self-managed associations rather than the state; contemporary adherents split on whether to defend state provision in the meantime.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Social anarchists reject capitalist markets as a source of exploitation, though they oppose state allocation too and the mutualist minority keeps markets among co-operatives.

public-ownership.rationale: Anarchists want the means of production held in common by producers and communes, but they reject nationalization by the state, so they agree only if public means society and not government.

unions-good.rationale: Unions organized for direct action are central to anarcho-syndicalism, which sees them as the seed of a free society, and anarchists have long built and supported labour unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Proudhon's 'property is theft' and the communist and collectivist demand for common ownership make rejection of private property in land and capital a defining anarchist position.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale turns on whether regulation should be tighter than now, or on replacing corporations instead of regulating them, and the statement now asks whether corporations should face strict government regulation.

reviewHistory.rationale: Anarchists oppose corporations as hierarchical institutions and want them replaced by self-management; they would curb corporate power, but distrust state regulation as the remedy.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale turns on whether regulation should be tighter than now, or on replacing corporations instead of regulating them, and the statement now asks whether corporations should face strict government regulation.

cut-welfare.rationale: Anarchists reject the idea that the poor are made dependent by aid, attributing poverty to capitalism and property, and they favour solidarity and mutual aid over cuts, though they do not idealize state welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: Workers' collective ownership and self-management of production is a core goal shared by mutualists, collectivists, communists and syndicalists.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anarchists see police and state security as core instruments of domination, so expanding state surveillance for any reason is rejected.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anarchists reject laws that govern individuals' private conduct, holding that law protects privilege rather than people, so they oppose prohibition of drug use by adults.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anarchists oppose giving the state power to censor, preferring to confront bigots and fascists through direct community action and antifascist organizing.

strong-leader.rationale: Rejection of rulers and of any concentrated authority over others is the definition of anarchism.

state-harmful.rationale: Abolishing the state, seen as an instrument of domination serving privileged minorities, is the defining anarchist aim.

limit-guns.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state's monopoly on force and have relied on armed popular self-defence and militias, as in the Spanish Revolution, while also being anti-militarist.

empower-police-military.rationale: Malatesta names the police, soldier and prison as the essential instruments of government, and anarchists are anti-militarist.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Anarchists oppose state control over consenting adults' bodies and sexuality, though classical anarchists such as Goldman treated prostitution as a product of economic exploitation to be ended by social change.

decide-locally.rationale: Decentralization and federation from the bottom up, with decisions made by local assemblies of those affected, is basic to anarchist organization.

rehabilitation.rationale: Anarchists see crime as largely produced by property and privilege and want prisons abolished; between the two options they reject punishment, though they also reject the prison itself.

traditional-family.rationale: Anarchists and anarcha-feminists treat the patriarchal family as a source of authoritarian conditioning and seek its replacement by free unions between equals.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anarcha-feminists hold that women must control their own bodies and reproduction, as in Goldman's call that women bear children only when they want them.

more-religion-public.rationale: Most anarchists are atheists who see religion as a justification of earthly authority, following Bakunin's rejection of God as master; Christian anarchism is a minority strand.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anarchists oppose all forms of domination, including racial hierarchy and colonialism, and Black and decolonizing anarchism are recognized strands; they pursue this through social struggle rather than state programs.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Anarchists reject nationalism and hold that the state creates the nation, while respecting cultures and the self-determination of oppressed peoples.

gradual-change.rationale: Social anarchists, the large majority, seek revolution against state and capital rather than gradual reform, but Malatesta's later writings on gradualism complicate a flat rejection, so this is the documented majority view.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anarchist opposition to nations and borders leads to solidarity with migrants and campaigns against deportations and border controls.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Bodies like the UN are associations of states; anarchists prefer federations of free associations ('world governance') to any world government.

free-trade.rationale: Anarchists oppose capitalist globalization, prominently in the anti-WTO protests, as serving capital rather than workers, while also opposing national protectionism.

nation-first.rationale: Anarchists reject patriotism and national interest as ideology serving the ruling classes, and are internationalist.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anarchists are anti-militarist and oppose wars waged by states, which they see as serving state and capitalist interests; a few, like Kropotkin in 1914, broke with this.

open-borders.rationale: A world of 'no borders and no nations' follows directly from the abolition of the state and is an explicit anarchist aim.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Anarchists hold that social problems stem from hierarchy and property, which technology alone cannot fix; social ecology accepts appropriate technology while primitivists reject it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Social revolution to overthrow state and capital is the main anarchist strategy, from Bakunin and Kropotkin onward.

experts-over-public.rationale: Anarchists accept experts as advisers but deny them any power to compel; authority must rest with those affected.

central-planning.rationale: Anarchists reject centralized state economic control as a new instrument of tyranny and favour decentralized federations of producers.

socialized-markets.rationale: Mutualists favour markets among worker co-operatives and collectivists accept exchange for a time, while anarchist communists want to abolish markets but see worker ownership as a precondition.

basic-income.rationale: An unconditional income from the state conflicts with anti-statism and with communists' aim to abolish money, but some contemporary anarchists support it as relief; adherents are split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Anarchists reject state control of the economy, holding production should be directed by federated producers' associations.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Mutualists and individualists favour small producers' possession of their means of work, while the social anarchist majority prefers collective possession and warns that individual ownership can recreate bosses and landlords.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Most social anarchists aim to abolish wage labour, which they call wage slavery, and look forward to ending money and buying and selling; mutualists are the exception.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Anarchists would abolish central banks with the state, but most reject leaving money to the market, aiming instead at mutual banks or the end of money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies uniting employers and workers contradict both anarchist anti-statism and the abolition of the employer class.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anarchists reject any party ruling the state, which they see as government by a new privileged minority.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Anarchism rejects all forms of rule, from monarchies to republics.

democracy-best.rationale: Anarchists reject representative government and majority rule as forms of domination and call universal suffrage a mockery, though most support direct democracy in self-managed assemblies.

direct-votes.rationale: Anarchists favour decisions by assemblies of those affected rather than representatives, though they reject laws themselves and majority votes binding on dissenting minorities.

workers-councils.rationale: Anarchists favour federations of workplace and community assemblies and unions over parliaments, though they reject any 'political power' as such.

right-to-secede.rationale: Free association includes the right to withdraw; anarchists hold that minorities may secede and that federations rest on voluntary agreement.

natural-rulers.rationale: Anarchists hold that no one should dominate another; human differences must never be turned into power.

political-violence-never.rationale: Most anarchists are not pacifists and accept revolutionary violence as a minimized 'necessary evil' and in self-defence, while anarcho-pacifists dissent.

war-builds-character.rationale: Anarchists are anti-militarist and see war as serving states and capital.

separate-church-state.rationale: Anarchists want neither state nor church authority and are strongly anti-clerical where churches hold power, so they reject any union of the two.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Anarchists reject laws as such and religion as a basis of authority; even Christian anarchists reject state law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Social anarchists reject capitalist firms as hierarchical and want defence and dispute resolution handled by free associations and arbitration; Tucker's individualist minority accepted private defence associations.

military-superiority.rationale: Anarchists are anti-militarist and internationalist, rejecting national military power.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Anarchists reject nationalism and ethnic discrimination and aim at a world without nations.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Most anarchists organize around class struggle against exploitation but reject Marxist economic determinism, also stressing the state, authority and mutual aid as historical forces.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Anarchists seek social equality and communists distribute by need, which goes beyond equal opportunity, though they reject identical treatment of unequal individuals.

civilizational-union.rationale: Anarchists reject political union based on religion or civilization as another form of state and nationalist identity.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Social anarchists see solidarity as enlightened self-interest and the egoist strand embraces self-interest outright, while rejecting capitalist individualism; adherents are split on framing it as a moral good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Anarchists put individual freedom from domination first and reject obligations imposed by a community, though they see individuality as developed socially.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Green anarchists and deep ecologists affirm nature's intrinsic value, while social ecology, the most influential current, rejects deep ecology as anti-human; split.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Primitivists hold this, but most anarchists reject primitivism as unrealistic and blame hierarchy and capitalism rather than civilization itself.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anarchists reject state surveillance and support privacy and security culture against state power.

restore-past-order.rationale: Anarchists seek a new, stateless and classless society, not the restoration of past hierarchies.

direct-action.rationale: Anarchists reject electoral politics as reinforcing state power and favour strikes, direct action and building alternative institutions, as Kropotkin and Malatesta set out.

means-match-ends.rationale: Anarchists hold that a free society can only be built by non-hierarchical means, the 'unity of means and ends' that set them against the Marxist road through state power.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitivists reject civilization, but mainstream social anarchists such as Kropotkin envisage a decentralised, technologically advanced society and most reject primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kropotkin called for combining agricultural, industrial and intellectual work so no one is confined to one specialised task for life, though anarchists accept that people's talents lead them to different work.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Anarchist communism, the dominant social anarchist position since the 1880s, rests on 'to every man according to his needs'; Bakuninist collectivists instead paid by labour in the transition.

production-for-use.rationale: Kropotkin argues that production must be organised to meet society's needs instead of the speculator's profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Anarchists hold that owners enrich themselves through the wage system and usury, meaning profits, rent and interest taken from labour.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anarchists split from Marxists precisely over this, holding that any workers' state becomes a new ruling class.

collective-farming.rationale: Social anarchists want land held in common and worked by free associations, as in the Spanish collectives, but reject forced collectivisation and allow individual farmers who work the land themselves.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anarchists are anti-militarist and see war as serving states and capital, though they blame the state as much as capitalism.

harm-principle.rationale: Anarchists reject laws that govern consenting adults' private conduct, but they deny the state any power at all, including the harm-prevention role the statement grants it.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individualist anarchists put the individual's rights against all groups, while social anarchists stress communal good and some support collective national liberation; anarchists are split.

conscription.rationale: Anarchists are anti-militarist, oppose the state's army and have long agitated against military service.

state-as-business.rationale: Anarchists oppose both the state and capitalist ownership, so a state owned and run like a company is doubly rejected.

organic-representation.rationale: Anarchists reject parties and would organise society through federations of communes and workers' associations, though they want mandated delegates rather than corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: Anarchism seeks to abolish the state altogether.

national-rebirth.rationale: Anarchists reject nationalism and patriotism as ideologies of the ruling classes.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Anarchists are anti-imperialist and anti-militarist and reject state borders altogether.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Anarchists oppose all hierarchical authority, including personal lordship.

bound-labor.rationale: Anarchists oppose all forced labour and want land free to those who work it.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anarchists oppose all states and nationalisms, and Israeli anarchists question Jewish nationalism and organise in joint struggle with Palestinians.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Anarchists call for workplaces run by those who work in them, with equal say for all members, though they seek self-management without bosses or owners rather than board seats within capitalist firms.

economic-freedom.rationale: Anarchists see capitalist property and wage labour as forms of domination that undermine freedom, so for them political freedom requires ending, not protecting, market economic 'freedom'.

rule-by-example.rationale: Anarchists reject rule itself and hold that authority corrupts rulers as well as the ruled, so they would not rely on rulers' example; they also reject laws and punishments, so the rejection of the statement is partial.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anarchists reject the nation-state and say the state creates the nation, but they back the liberation of oppressed peoples, so they deny a right to a state while supporting self-rule.

force-without-un.rationale: Anarchists oppose states, armies and militarism and reject wars waged by governments, whether or not an international body approves them.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Most anarchists are atheists who follow Bakunin in rejecting divine authority and appeal to science and reason, but religious anarchists exist and emotion and solidarity matter, so the agreement is not total.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Anarchists reject nations and borders and hold that people living and working somewhere share equally in common resources, so citizenship-based limits on benefits contradict their internationalism.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social anarchists hold that real freedom requires equality and the means to live, which is why they seek common ownership and distribution by need.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Anarchists reject state-imposed conditions and want needs met by free association and distribution according to need, not compelled labor.

class-collaboration.rationale: Anarchists call wage labor wage slavery and seek to abolish the wage system and capitalism rather than make peace with employers.

dominated-front.rationale: Anarchists support anti-colonial struggle but distrust state and nationalist fronts, so they are split.

workers-nation.rationale: Anarchism is internationalist and critical of nationalism and borders, and organizes workers across nations as a class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Anarchists oppose patriarchy and have an anarcha-feminist strand, and they reject law imposing roles on anyone.

ban-interest.rationale: Anarchists reject state coercion and law as such, so a legal ban on lending is contrary to their approach.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Anarchists oppose hierarchy and the state's power to classify and coerce, and stand in solidarity with migrants against nationalism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Anarchists hold that the state exists to protect property and privilege and to exploit the many for the few.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Anarchists reject nationalism and borders and practice migrant solidarity, so demanding assimilation to a national culture runs against their core stance.

proportional-representation.rationale: Malatesta and the social anarchist tradition reject parliament and voting as a route to freedom, so tinkering with seat allocation is not their goal.

national-mission.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state and nationalism and are internationalist and anti-militarist, so exporting a national government is rejected.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anarchism extends its critique of hierarchy to patriarchy, and anarcha-feminism is an established strand.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anarchists hold that government is a class instrument that corrupts those who rule and serves privilege against ordinary people.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Anarchists seek to abolish the state altogether and see police and army as tools of exploitation and property.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Anarchists oppose nationalism and every hierarchy of group over group, and defend free choice in personal life.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anarchism rejects hierarchy and treats all people as equals, but it rejects state law, so 'rights before the law' is only partly its framing.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Anarchists defend free thought and oppose state coercion in matters of belief.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Bakunin's critique of Marxism held that a strong transitional state entrenches a new ruling class; anarchists want the state abolished at once.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Anarchists hold that only voluntary association is legitimate, though they reject the very idea of being governed.

population-transfer.rationale: Anarchists reject the state's power to expel anyone and are internationalist and anti-nationalist, defending free movement and the right of all to stay.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Anarchists oppose coercive hierarchy, but the mainstream accepts revolutionary violence and collective force against oppressors, and the non-aggression principle belongs to the individualist and libertarian strand.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Kropotkin's Mutual Aid argued that cooperation, not struggle, drives evolution and social progress, and anarchists reject competition as the basis of capitalist society.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anarchists hold that freedom is lost under any hierarchy or rulership, including wage dependence on a boss, whether or not power is exercised, which matches the non-domination view.

vanguard-party.rationale: Anarchists reject Leninist vanguardism and hold that workers must organize and liberate themselves through their own self-managed movements.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Direct action, including strikes and picketing, is the core anarchist method, and they reject the state as the body that would limit it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Kropotkin argues that modern production can supply abundance for all, so poverty comes from property and the wage system, not numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Anarchists critique nationalism and stress solidarity across ethnic lines, rejecting the idea that diversity breeds conflict.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Malatesta treats government and its emergency powers as the instrument of oppression, so suspending protections for state security is rejected.

party-controls-media.rationale: Anarchists oppose state or party control over information and defend free expression and association.

party-commands-army.rationale: Anarchists abolish the state and the standing army alike and are anti-militarist, so a party-commanded army is the opposite of their aims.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and critical of borders, so long waits for membership run against their position.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Anarchists reject government and standing armies altogether, so a ruler commanding the military is the opposite of their aim.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Anarchists oppose hierarchy in all institutions including churches, and are generally secular.

clerical-rule.rationale: Anarchists reject all rulers and are generally secular, so rule by religious authorities is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and anti-militarist and see wars between states as ruling-class conflicts, so they favor turning them against the rulers; the pacifist strand differs.

recall-officials.rationale: Where delegates exist, anarchists want them accountable and instantly recallable by those who sent them.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Anarchists oppose states' military machines, alliances and wars as instruments of rulers, and are internationalist and anti-militarist.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Anarchists attack landlordism, but they would end it by common occupancy and mutual aid rather than by law and universal family ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Anarchists reject standing armies and the state's monopoly of force, favoring voluntary armed militias of the people if defense is needed.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Anarchists oppose creating or enlarging nation-states and see nationalism as a statist doctrine, though some support national liberation struggles.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anarchists distrust rule by the learned (Bakunin) but prize education and are not anti-intellectual; adherents are split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Anarchists reject hierarchies among peoples and the nationalist ranking of cultures, and value cultural diversity.

death-penalty.rationale: Anarchists reject state killing and punishment as authority's tools and favor addressing the causes of crime.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anarchists are generally secular and oppose religious authority, and would not want creation accounts put in school science.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Anarchists reject citizenship as a state category and favor open borders, so neither rule is theirs, but birthright is the less exclusive one.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Anarchists reject special legal privileges and oppose religion's authority, yet defend liberty of practice; adherents are split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Anarchism prizes individual liberty and critiques social as well as legal coercion, though it also stresses solidarity and mutual aid.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anarchists hold that national liberation without abolishing state and capital only swaps rulers, as Gordon sets out.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Anarchists reject any assembly that governs through representative state power, preferring federated self-managed councils, as Malatesta rejects parliament and suffrage.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Anarchists reject coercive authority, hold that freedom and equality are inseparable, and oppose any state limiting liberties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state and its army, as Kropotkin and Malatesta set out, and are anti-militarist and internationalist.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Anarchists reject the office of head of state and electoral politics as reinforcing state power.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and reject nationalism and borders, so they reject holding territory as a historic homeland.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Kropotkin holds that property should be held in common and production should serve needs, so ownership serves the community.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anarchists hold that the USSR replaced the old rulers with a bureaucratic state that kept wage labour, and rejected the Bolshevik path.

collective-defense.rationale: Anarchists reject armies, states and alliances as instruments of domination and are anti-militarist.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Anarchists abolish the state and its offices, so a state figurehead has no place however non-partisan.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Anarchists hold that free association includes the right to secede and reject coercion by states.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers and religion's claims to authority.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Anarchists oppose rulers and government as such, and a ruler above the law is the extreme case.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Anarchists reject rule by the few and by representatives, and in favour of direct democracy and federation.

leader-cult.rationale: Anarchists oppose hierarchy and the deference to rulers that a leader cult embodies.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Anarchists from Bakunin on warned that a socialist party state would form a new ruling class, so struggle continues.

land-redistribution.rationale: Social anarchists call for expropriating landowners and common use of land by those who work it.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Anarchism rejects nationalism and state claims on territory.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Anarchism is secular and opposes coercive law over belief.

women-must-cover.rationale: Anarchism opposes state coercion and patriarchy, so dress laws for women are rejected.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Anarchism is internationalist and rejects unity based on nationality or ancestry.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Anarchism is internationalist and opposes closed economic blocs and colonies.

moral-incentives.rationale: Kropotkin's communism seeks to end wage labour and rest work on solidarity and voluntary duty.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Anarchists are split between mass revolution and insurrectionary minority action.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Anarchism opposes all coercive hierarchy, including inherited rank and privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anarchists reject all rule of one people or person over another, and oppose colonial domination as a form of the state and hierarchy.

patriotic-education.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state and nationalism and are anti-militarist, so teaching loyalty to the nation, flag and anthem is rejected as indoctrination.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anarchists oppose empire, state power and nationalism, so cultivating imperial-style influence is rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Social anarchists reject hierarchy and domination including racial and sexual, and tie freedom to equality, so licence to discriminate through property power is rejected; the anarcho-capitalist view is excluded from scope.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and its borders, and oppose colonialism; the anarchist-nationalism entry notes support for anti-colonial struggle.

elective-rulers.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers altogether, whether inherited or elected, and see elections as reinforcing state power.

minority-veto.rationale: Anarchist decision-making rests on voluntary association and consensus, so no one is bound without consent, though the FAQ accepts majority rule in some cases.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Anarchists oppose parliaments and all state authority, as Kropotkin's Anarchy argues against suffrage and parliament.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Anarchists reject hierarchy and charity from above in favour of mutual aid among equals, as the FAQ stresses.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Anarchism is an activist movement of direct action, and it builds alternative institutions rather than withdrawing.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Anarchists hold that media and culture help sustain hierarchical social order, as in the critique of state, church and capital.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Anarchist theory holds that states and capitalists rule partly through ideology and institutions, not force alone.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anarchists, as anti-capitalists and internationalists, hold that capitalism and the state extract surplus from workers and poor regions.

native-born-offices.rationale: Anarchists reject states, borders and nationalism, so reserving offices for natives is contrary to their internationalism.

party-own-road.rationale: Anarchists reject party-led paths to socialism entirely; independence from foreign parties is not the issue they address.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Anarchists reject states, borders and nationalism, so demanding territory for a state contradicts their core principles.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Anarchists reject rule of any group over another, including by ancestry, though they support indigenous autonomy and anti-colonial struggle.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anarchists are split: they oppose all authoritarian states, but the anarchist left rejects equating fascism with communism's varied history.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anarchist and left scholarship holds slavery was the central cause of the Civil War.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its negative rests on rejecting the idea that other civilizations should develop their own forms of government, and the statement now asks only whether Western institutions are unsuitable for some civilizations.

reviewHistory.rationale: Anarchists reject Western state institutions altogether; they see all states as illegitimate rather than any model as civilisation-specific.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Anarchists oppose the army and state as instruments of coercion and are anti-militarist.

office-by-exam.rationale: Anarchists reject rule by officials altogether and want administration by self-managed associations, so selecting an official class by examination is opposed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Free association is central, so either partner may leave a relationship without needing state-defined grounds.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Anarchists favour direct democracy with mandated delegates who are recallable at any time, in place of independent representatives.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private companies running individual retirement accounts embody the wage system and capitalism; Kropotkin calls for distribution according to need.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Kropotkin and social anarchists want land and the means of production held in common and used by those who work them; the nation is not their unit, so only partial agreement.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Anarchists reject borders and nationalism and stress migrant solidarity, so barring foreigners from owning land is opposed.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Anarchists oppose states and their armies; arming rebels for state interests is a use of state power they reject, though they back some liberation movements.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and anti-militarist and oppose state domination, so troops imposing a bloc's order are rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anarchists see the state and capital as allied hierarchies, so corporate capture of government is expected, though they would not fix it through reform.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Anarchists reject the claim that government has legitimate authority over the individual, so there is no general obligation to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: Anarchists oppose state intervention yet support solidarity with oppressed peoples across borders, so they split.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Anarchists oppose nationalism and scapegoating of minorities, and they are generally internationalist and anti-racist.

local-production.rationale: Kropotkin favoured decentralised, locally integrated production, though globalised mutual aid is also accepted.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anarchist strands favour small affinity groups and federations built from below, although social anarchists also build unions and federations.

religious-nation.rationale: Anarchists are generally secular and oppose nationalism, so defining a nation by religion is contrary to their position.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anarchists reject hierarchy among individuals and among states and oppose tribute and domination.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Social anarchists distribute by need through federations of free communes, not by regions hoarding revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Social anarchists seek common ownership of land, factories and tools but not of personal belongings.

religion-illusion.rationale: Anarchists are generally atheist and see religion as part of the structure of authority, and expect it to wane as domination ends; some religious anarchists differ.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anarchist critique of hierarchy includes patriarchy and capitalism together, so economic transformation is part of equality.

treaties-binding.rationale: Anarchists reject state treaties as such but support the self-determination of peoples, so no clear answer.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Anarchists want society federated from self-governing communes holding property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Anarchists oppose nationalism and state-steered domination of minorities.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anarchists reject both capitalism and state communism in favor of libertarian socialism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Anarchists reject nations and territorial states as bases of legitimacy, so a people's ancestral or religious tie to land confers no privileged claim over those living there now.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anarchist opposition to state coercion over personal life and to enforced moral conformity means consensual adult relations are no business of the law.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Anarchism's core is opposition to authority imposed by force; suppressing dissent for the sake of order is the state behaviour it condemns, and it values free association and free criticism.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Classical anarchists (Bakunin especially) were anticlerical and opposed any state power over belief; a government punishing blasphemy or false worship is doubly objectionable.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anarchists oppose both the state and imperial domination, rejecting rule of one people over another for the rulers' economic gain.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct, face-to-face decision-making in workplaces, communes and federated assemblies is central to social anarchist organisation, in place of rule by distant officials.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Modern social anarchism opposes every hierarchy, not only class, and anarcha-feminist and anti-racist currents treat these as linked, though classical writers stressed class and the state first.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Social anarchists see themselves as part of the libertarian socialist left, opposed to both capitalism and the state, so they do not accept merging left and right as a way forward.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anarchists condemn wage labour as wage slavery that subordinates workers and deny them control of their own work, and call for self-management.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist, reject nationalism and borders and show solidarity with migrants.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Anarchists reject all authority and are generally secular and atheist.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Anarchists want to abolish the state and oppose religion, but generally oppose coercive dress rules; no common view of this question.

social-market-economy.rationale: Social anarchists reject both capitalism and the state and seek common ownership and distribution by need.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anarchists oppose the army and police as tools of the state and are anti-militarist.

rich-first.rationale: Equality and abolition of exploitation are core, so letting some grow rich first contradicts them.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and all hierarchy, and Kropotkin and the FAQ oppose any inherited or imposed authority.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Proudhon-style mutualists favor mutual banks, while communist anarchists abolish money altogether, so strands split.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anarchists oppose capitalist globalization and institutions like the IMF, as in the anti-globalization movement, though they want no state-run alternative.

property-franchise.rationale: Anarchists reject hierarchy and wealth-based privilege, and want equal participation in self-managed bodies, not property tests.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Anarcha-feminism and green anarchism, notably social ecology, tie domination of women and nature to one logic of hierarchy.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Malatesta argued that political liberties are hollow without economic equality, and the FAQ makes the same point about wealth and power.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Anarchists reject rulers and statute law and judges alike, favoring free agreement and custom, though they do prefer fixed rules to arbitrary decrees.

racial-franchise.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and reject nationalism and ethnic hierarchy, and Gordon documents their opposition to borders and ethnic exclusion.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Anarchists are generally secular, oppose state regulation of private life, and favor free association among adults.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and solidaristic with minorities and migrants, so religious boycotts are rejected.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Anarchists attack private accumulation of wealth as a source of domination and exploitation, and seek common ownership so no one can command others through wealth.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Anarchists seek to abolish the state and its coercive institutions, including police and prisons, in favour of voluntary and community arrangements.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Anarchists favour mutual aid and common ownership over both state aid and hierarchical charity, so the claim as worded is not their view; Kropotkin stresses mutual aid.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Anarchists oppose patriarchy and domination, extending their critique to the family, so male authority in marriage is rejected.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Anarchism is anti-militarist and opposes hierarchy, obedience and state or movement control of the young.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anarchists are anti-militarist and oppose state weapons and armies in general, so they oppose hosting nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anarchists are anti-militarist and oppose foreign armies, though they reject the sovereignty framing and the national state.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anarchists condemn mass killings but distrust state declarations and do not look to governments for official recognition; adherents differ.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Proudhon and Kropotkin attack rent, interest and profit as unearned, and call for common ownership so that labour is not exploited by owners.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The social anarchist majority accepts defensive and revolutionary violence; pacifist anarchists are a separate strand the audit does not follow.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Gordon shows anarchists treat nations as constructed and inherently tied to state power, not as continuous from antiquity.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Anarchists oppose nationalism and the sacralising of the nation and state, though they remember their own movement's martyrs.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Anarchism is generally secular and treats politics as a struggle against domination and hierarchy, not a spiritual war.

culture-before-state.rationale: Anarchists seek to abolish the state altogether, so the sequencing of culture and state-building does not arise; adherents differ on cultural self-determination.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Anarchism is generally secular, so it does not adopt a test for religious texts; anarcha-feminists criticise religious patriarchy but do not set a standard.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and reject nationalism, so tying economic life to a national majority contradicts their principles.

independent-unions.rationale: Anarchists want workers' organisations that are self-managed and free of any state or party, which is why they rejected Marxist party control of unions.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Anarchists want these services run in common by communities and workers rather than the state, so they split on whether 'public hands' means the state.

second-chamber.rationale: Anarchists reject parliaments and legislatures; federal delegates are mandated and recallable, so a second chamber is not a feature of their model.

municipal-property.rationale: Social anarchists hold the means of production in common through communes and workers' associations, though they also stress federations of such associations, not only the locality.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Kropotkin and the FAQ describe free federation from the bottom up, with mandated, recallable delegates coordinating and decisions staying with local assemblies.

person-over-state.rationale: Anarchists see the state as an instrument of domination and defend individual freedom against it, though they also stress that freedom is realised through association.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Anarchism is generally secular and Malatesta criticises religion, though religious anarchists exist and are a minority.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Anarchists reject a national legislature that holds power over regions; self-government rests on free federation and the right of secession.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Anarchists are anti-militarist and want armies abolished, so they would not endorse any state's armed forces even for defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Anarchists treat nations as constructed communities tied to states and reject nationalism, so language alone is not a basis for a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Anarchists reject elections and state representation altogether, and the separation of people by religious community cuts against free association.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Anarchists oppose nationalism and see state power as the problem, so they do not frame politics as defence of a country against foreign plots.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: Anarcha-feminists attack patriarchy, but many anarchists reject claims that women share distinct values as essentialist.

arms-reduction.rationale: Anarchism is anti-militarist and wants armies abolished, so it agrees with cuts though it rejects the national-safety framing.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Anarchists reject state diplomacy as a whole, so the question of open treaties between governments is not theirs.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and its monopoly of force, and favour an armed, self-organised people over standing armies and police.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Anti-militarism is core: anarchists see state wars as fought for rulers and urge soldiers and conscripts to refuse.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Anarchists hold the state must be abolished by revolution, not captured, which is the classic split with Marxist parties.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Malatesta and the 'anarchism without adjectives' view leave economic forms to free experiment, though most social anarchists favour common ownership.

sacred-nation.rationale: Anarchism rejects nationalism and statism as forms of domination, and is generally secular and internationalist.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Kropotkin grounds mutual aid in human nature, but Bakunin and later anarchists treat human traits as socially shaped; adherents are split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Anarchists reject electoral politics and party participation as reinforcing state power, favouring direct action and abstentionism.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Anarchism has no doctrine on how languages are named; it favours cultural autonomy and opposes nationalism, which points both ways.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Anarchism rejects hierarchical authority and any formal lawmaking body, traditional or elected.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Social anarchists claim freedom and ecology are compatible, while the green strand is split on constraint; adherents are divided.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist, oppose nationalism and borders, and reject state-imposed requirements on newcomers.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Anarchists build on free association, so compulsory membership or dues sit badly with it, though some syndicalists defend union solidarity.

voter-id.rationale: Anarchists reject the electoral state, and ID-gated voting adds state control to a process they already see as hollow.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Anarchists abolish the state and its coercive hierarchy, so no religious interpretation could hold legal authority.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Malatesta and the FAQ hold that electing rulers does not make society self-governing; real democracy is direct, participatory and non-hierarchical.

premarital-sex.rationale: Anarcha-feminism and the anarchist critique of marriage and authority support sexual freedom for women.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Anarchists want the wage system and the state abolished, not softened by a state-run cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Anarchists demand equal rights for women, though they reject voting and office-holding as a route to change.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Anarchists are generally secular and see religion as one of the institutions of hierarchy, and anarcha-feminists link it to patriarchy.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Social anarchists hold that property rests on use and occupancy, not first claim, and reject permanent private ownership of land and resources.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Anarchism is generally atheist and anti-clerical ('no gods, no masters'), and rejects religious authority over life and thought.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state in any form, including the Bolshevik state, and see state socialism as a new ruling class rather than something to defend.

indirect-election.rationale: Anarchist federalism builds higher bodies from mandated, recallable delegates of lower councils, not from popular election of rulers.

national-church-status.rationale: Anarchists oppose both state and church privilege, so a legally privileged national church is rejected.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Anarchists favour self-determination of communities but reject state sovereignty and plebiscites as state instruments, so adherents split.

simple-living.rationale: Tolstoyan, green and primitivist strands praise simple living but communist anarchists stress abundance for all; mainstream is split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Anarchists reject nationalism and treat a nation's claim on land as a ground for domination, favouring internationalism and open solidarity across borders.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Anarchists see police and army as instruments of oppression and oppose state killing of any kind, though they also reject state courts and prisons.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Anarchists reject national-kin loyalties and state intervention on their behalf, backing solidarity with all migrants and minorities instead.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Social anarchists hold land and the means of production in common and reject private appropriation, though they expect commons to be run by associations rather than by compensation schemes.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Anarchists reject any leader ruling over the people and build direct, federated, self-managed organisations rather than leaving politics to a leader.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Anarchists see government as the protector of property and privilege for the propertied, and want no state favours to capital.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Anarchists are generally secular and reject religious authority in public life, though they also reject parliaments and offices altogether.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Anarchism holds relationships should be free associations and anarcha-feminism opposes patriarchal marriage law, so either partner may leave.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Social anarchists hold that property and capital are products of exploitation and want common ownership, so an unequal distribution is unjust even if reached by voluntary exchange.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Anarchists deny the state's claim to authority, so a law's legal form does not bind them; justice and conscience are the guide.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Kropotkin argued that machinery should free people from toil and let all work less, a view carried into anarchist communism.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Anarchism opposes nationalism and borders as forms of domination and is internationalist.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Anarchists reject the state, parties and capitalism alike, so party-led socialism with markets contradicts their aims.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Anarchists reject the idea that the poor are made dependent by aid, attributing poverty to capitalism and property, and they favour solidarity and mutual aid over cuts, though they do not idealize state welfare. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Anarchists oppose empire, state power and nationalism, so cultivating imperial-style influence is rejected. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Political change should come through direct action outside elections and parliaments rather than through them.
missingStatements.rationale: Anarchists reject electoral politics as reinforcing state power, with the Bakuninist tradition practising abstentionism and favouring strikes, direct action and building alternative institutions.

missingStatements.text: The methods used to change society should themselves reflect the society one wants to create.
missingStatements.rationale: Anarchists hold that a free society can only be built by non-hierarchical means and build self-managed institutions now, which is why they rejected the Marxist path through state power.

notes: Individualist and mutualist anarchists would answer more favourably on markets, small property and self-interest; anarcho-pacifists and Christian anarchists would reject revolutionary violence; primitivists would agree that industrial civilization has been a disaster. Many policy statements presuppose state action that anarchists reject in principle, so those answers reflect the direction anarchists favour, not support for the state carrying it out.
